item: Doubled-Fano gadget with its all-CAT(0) finite obstruction (P03+P47), plus the uniform conditional test (P37), for a hyperbolic group without a geometric CAT(0) action
item_type: F3 (gadget + finite obstruction, a witness design) / F5 (uniform conditional test, a lemma)
analyst_note: Text-level work only. The Lean was not compiled (no local toolchain). Web tools hit their session quota early in this pass; every outside reference marked [unverified] comes from memory or from a subagent summary and must be checked before use.
lean_status_why: All three parts of the item are in the Lean and on the comparator's dependency path (template carrier `Field`/`Edge`, `no_finite_obstruction`, `SamplingSequence.conditional`). The conditional test follows the paper, but the finite obstruction is proved by a shorter algebraic tangent-cone route without the paper's CAT(1) local-geodesic and parallel-set theorems. The comparator is weaker than the paper's Thm 1.1 at the statement level only, and both omitted clauses are within a few dozen lines of what the Lean already proves.

lean_gaps.gap: Comparator omits '2-dimensional' (paper Thm 1.1: 'finite connected two-dimensional aspherical simplicial complex').
lean_gaps.detail: The Lean witness is `finalFiniteComplex m = elementaryFiniteComplex … = toFiniteComplex (elementaryPolygonData …).complex` (IndexedFillingValue.lean:5335, 2950). For the underlying polygon model the Lean already proves `FinitePolygonModel.Data.simplex_card_le_three` (FinitePolygonModel.lean:94): every face has at most 3 vertices, i.e. dimension at most 2. What is missing is only (a) transporting that bound through `toFiniteComplex`, which is a reindexing along `Fintype.equivFin` (IndexedFillingValue.lean:2887) and preserves face cardinalities, (b) one 3-vertex face to get dimension exactly 2 (any `collarFace` of a cell works), and (c) adding the clause to `MainStatement`. Text-level estimate: 20–40 new lines. So the omission is a statement-level choice, not a missing proof.

lean_gaps.gap: Comparator omits the locally CAT(0) model clause. It excludes only compatible locally CAT(−1) metrics (`CompatibleLocallyCATNegOne`), which is strictly weaker because a locally CAT(−1) metric is locally CAT(0).
lean_gaps.detail: The CAT(−1) clause is proved by `homotopy_incompatibleLocalCATNegOne` → `incompatibleLocalCATNegOne_of_noAction` → `not_noGeometricCATZeroAction_of_compact_localCATNegOne` (CompactLocalCATGeometric.lean). The only place CAT(−1) is used is `uniformLocalCATZero_of_compact` (IndexedFillingValue.lean:7037). It applies a Lebesgue number and then `(hc y).catZero` (`CATNegOne.catZero`, IndexedFillingValue.lean:6978) to get `UniformLocalCATZero r`. Everything downstream (the development, deck action, properness and CAT(0)-ness of the developed cover in DevelopmentDeck/DevelopmentProper/DevelopmentGeometricAction/LocalGeodesic) takes only `UniformLocalCATZero r`. A `CompatibleLocallyCATZero L` with `CATZero (ball x r)` in place of `CATNegOne` can therefore be excluded by copying three lemmas and deleting the `.catZero` call: about 30–50 lines. With that, the comparator would imply the paper's statement, since the CAT(−1) exclusion follows from the CAT(0) one.

lean_gaps.gap: Infinitude dropped from `MainStatement` (`exists_finite_aspherical_hyperbolic_noAction` proves `Infinite π₁`, and `main` discards it with `_`).
lean_gaps.detail: Harmless. A finite group acts geometrically on a one-point CAT(0) space, so `NoGeometricCATZeroAction` already forces π₁K to be infinite. This also rules out the trivial-group loophole in `WordHyperbolic`.

lean_gaps.gap: Different route for the finite obstruction (P47).
lean_gaps.detail: Paper Sec 6 uses tangent cones, flat rigidity, antipodality via the CAT(1) local-geodesic theorem, and a splitting of the parallel set of the M_C/M_D axis. The Lean (`no_finite_obstruction`, CATZeroFurther.lean:212) builds the completed tangent cone (`TangentCone.coneData`) and then argues purely algebraically. It uses `fan_identity`, `exceptional_identity`, `ConeData.exceptional_antipodes` ('in an algebraic form that avoids a local-to-global theorem in the completed space of directions', CATZero.lean:463) and `five_line_fans_contradiction`. Same conclusion, shorter proof, no parallel-set theorem.

lean_gaps.gap: Uniform conditional test: same statement, quantitative and limit forms are split.
lean_gaps.detail: Paper P37 (05-energy.tex:246-295) is a limsup statement uniform over actions chosen after the tables. The Lean splits it into the finite quantitative bound `ConeData.conditional_test` (FiniteLaw.lean:111), with explicit coupling errors B·√(1/(n+1)+2M²η)+2BMη, and the limit `SamplingSequence.conditional` (ConditionalStar.lean:147) via `conditional_test_eventually`. Uniformity is expressed structurally: `SamplingSequence` carries only combinatorial data, and `conditional` holds for every later sequence of `EnergyOrbit`s `O`. The displacement bound is M = 8 (paper: generic M). No weakening found.
`finalFinite_noAction` is an `∀ᶠ m in atTop` statement, and `main` uses `.exists`, so no explicit K is produced (the paper says the same, 01:15).

lean_gaps.gap: Other Lean route differences (not affecting the item).
lean_gaps.detail: Asphericity is proved by an explicit contraction of the universal cover (paper: Hurewicz + Whitehead). Infinitude is proved by a six-cell rank count (paper: Euler characteristic). The Lean also proves its own Cartan–Hadamard development and its own 'linear filling ⇒ four-point hyperbolic' (family.md).

comparator_chain_branches: Metric core via the conditional test: `MasterGraph.impossible_sequence` → `MasterGraph.metricCore` (GraphLimit.lean:109) → `MasterGraph.path_lower` → `SamplingSequence.limit_path` (OrbitLimit.lean) → `SamplingSequence.word_lower` (ConditionalStar.lean:300) → `SamplingSequence.conditional` (ConditionalStar.lean:147, call at :324) → `ConeData.conditional_test` (FiniteLaw.lean:111) + `conditional_test_eventually` (FiniteLaw.lean:195).

Exceptional ternary test via the conditional test: `MasterGraph.impossible_sequence` → `MasterGraph.exceptionalTest` (Exceptional.lean) → `SamplingSequence.limit_fractional` (OrbitLimit.lean:159) → `SamplingSequence.fractional_error` (ConditionalStar.lean:409) → `SamplingSequence.conditional` (call at :425).

Template carrier: the sampling labels are indexed by `IncidenceTemplate.Field = Edge ⊕ (TwoPath × Fin 2)` (Template.lean:36), with `Edge` = all Fano incidences on 11 representatives (A–D doubled) minus (10,4) = Y_D–CD (Template.lean:15). The same omission appears in `CoreGeometry.Adjacent` (MetricHexagon.lean:114), which `MetricCore` and `toObstruction` use. The novelty pass found Edge/Field to be dependencies of 42.7%/40.5% of the patched DAG.

CAT(−1) clause: `main` → `homotopy_incompatibleLocalCATNegOne` → `incompatibleLocalCATNegOne_of_noAction` → `not_noGeometricCATZeroAction_of_compact_localCATNegOne` → `uniformLocalCATZero_of_compact` + Cartan–Hadamard development. It reuses the no-action conclusion `hno` from the main path.

lean_source.text:
/-- All incidences except Y_D--CD. Both sides have fixed named positions. -/
abbrev Edge := {p : Fin 11 × Fin 7 // Incident (pointOfRepresentative p.1) p.2 ∧ p ≠ (10,4)}

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.IncidenceTemplate.isLoose
lean_source.text: def isLoose (e : Edge) : Prop := e.val = (3,4)

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.IncidenceTemplate.fan
lean_source.text:
def fan (i : Fin 7) : Finset Edge :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun e => pointOfRepresentative e.val.1 = i ∧ ¬isLoose e)

lean_source.text: lemma card_fan : ∀ i : Fin 7, (fan i).card = ![6,6,6,4,3,3,3] i

OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.IncidenceTemplate.Incident
lean_source.text:
/-- Lines are the kernels of the seven nonzero linear functionals. -/
def Incident (i l : Fin 7) : Prop := ∑ j, vector i j * vector l j = 0

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.CoreGeometry.Adjacent
lean_source.text:
def Adjacent : Vertex → Vertex → Prop
  | .inl r, .inr l => Incident (pointOfRepresentative r) l ∧ (r,l) ≠ (10,4)
  | .inr l, .inl r => Incident (pointOfRepresentative r) l ∧ (r,l) ≠ (10,4)
  | _, _ => False
instance (v w : Vertex) : Decidable (Adjacent v w) := by
  cases v <;> cases w <;> unfold Adjacent <;> infer_instance

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.CoreGeometry.MetricCore
lean_source.text:
/-- Exactly the core path distances in Proposition `configuration` (i).
The third condition uses distinct fields and the actual fan quota; the
exceptional loose edge is not charged to the D fan. -/
structure MetricCore {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (z : Vertex → X) : Prop where
  side : ∀ a b, Adjacent a b → dist (z a) (z b) ^ 2 = 1
  twoStep : ∀ a b c, Adjacent a b → Adjacent b c → a ≠ c →
    dist (z a) (z c) ^ 2 = 2
  threeStep : ∀ a b c d, Adjacent a b → Adjacent b c → Adjacent c d →
    a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ThreeQuota a b c d → 3 ≤ dist (z a) (z d) ^ 2

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.CoreGeometry.ExceptionalTest
lean_source.text:
/-- The three-field, two-fractional-geodesic inequality in the source's
configuration proposition, at the exceptional missing incidence. -/
def ExceptionalTest {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (h : CATZero X) (z : Vertex → X) : Prop :=
  ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1,
    t ^ 2 * (1 / 2 + 1) ≤
      dist (CATZero.segment h (z (.inr 4)) (CATZero.mid h (z (.inl 2)) (z (.inl 9))) t)
        (CATZero.segment h (z (.inr 4)) (z (.inl 3)) t) ^ 2

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.CoreGeometry.MetricCore.impossible
lean_source.text:
/-- No CAT(0) space contains the exact limiting core configuration of
Proposition `configuration`, including its exceptional fractional test. -/
theorem impossible (h : CATZero X) (he : ExceptionalTest h z) : False

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.fullLines
lean_source.text:
/-- Full incidences among the six lines AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD at A,B,C,D.
These are exactly the doubled fans of the source. -/
def fullLines : Fin 4 → Finset (Fin 6) :=
  ![{0, 1, 2}, {0, 3, 4}, {1, 3, 5}, {2, 4}]

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.FiniteObstructionData
lean_source.text:
/-- The specific subconfiguration used by the source obstruction. This is
metric input to a contradiction, not an assumed existence assertion. All its
conditions are consequences asserted by source Proposition `configuration`;
the existence-from-actions direction remains a separate obligation. -/
structure FiniteObstructionData {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (h : CATZero X) where
  c : X
  x : Fin 4 → X
  y : Fin 4 → X
  line : Fin 6 → X
  radiusX : ∀ i, dist c (x i) ^ 2 = 3 / 4
  radiusY : ∀ i, dist c (y i) ^ 2 = 3 / 4
  radiusLine : ∀ i, dist c (line i) ^ 2 = 3 / 4
  lineDist : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → dist (line a) (line b) ^ 2 = 2
  lineFlat : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → dist c (CATZero.mid h (line a) (line b)) ^ 2 = 1 / 4
  square : ∀ i a b, a ∈ fullLines i → b ∈ fullLines i → a ≠ b →
    MetricSquare (x i) (line a) (y i) (line b)
  twoStepX : dist (x 2) (x 3) ^ 2 = 2
  twoStepY : dist (y 2) (x 3) ^ 2 = 2
  loose : dist (line 5) (x 3) ^ 2 = 1
  missing : 3 ≤ dist (y 3) (line 5) ^ 2
  fractional : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1,
    t ^ 2 * (1 / 2 + 1) ≤
      dist (CATZero.segment h (line 5) (CATZero.mid h (x 2) (y 2)) t)
        (CATZero.segment h (line 5) (x 3) t) ^ 2

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.no_finite_obstruction
lean_source.text:
/-- The complete finite CAT(0) metric obstruction from Section 6. The proof
constructs the completed tangent cone and all rigidity identities internally. -/
theorem no_finite_obstruction {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (h : CATZero X)
    (D : FiniteObstructionData h) : False

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.TangentCone.fan_identity
lean_source.text:
/-- The fan midpoint identity, derived from a metric square and the central
flatness of its line diagonal. -/
theorem fan_identity (c x y a b : X)
    (hcx : dist c x ^ 2 = 3 / 4) (hcy : dist c y ^ 2 = 3 / 4)
    (hca : dist c a ^ 2 = 3 / 4) (hcb : dist c b ^ 2 = 3 / 4)
    (hxa : dist x a ^ 2 = 1) (hay : dist a y ^ 2 = 1)
    (hyb : dist y b ^ 2 = 1) (hbx : dist b x ^ 2 = 1)
    (hxy : dist x y ^ 2 = 2) (hab : dist a b ^ 2 = 2)
    (hflat : dist c (CATZero.mid h a b) ^ 2 = 1 / 4) :
    (coneData h c).pairing (log h c x) (log h c y) = -1 / 4 ∧
    (coneData h c).add (catZero h c) (log h c x) (log h c y) =
      (coneData h c).add (catZero h c) (log h c a) (log h c b)

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.TangentCone.exceptional_identity
lean_source.text:
/-- Source exceptional-incidence identity. Its hypotheses are entirely metric,
including the fixed-fraction test; no flat triangle or cone identity is assumed. -/
theorem exceptional_identity (c p q z k : X)
    (hcp : dist c p ^ 2 = 3 / 4) (hcq : dist c q ^ 2 = 3 / 4)
    (hcz : dist c z ^ 2 = 3 / 4) (hck : dist c k ^ 2 = 3 / 4)
    (hpq : dist p q ^ 2 = 2) (hpz : dist p z ^ 2 = 2) (hqz : dist q z ^ 2 = 2)
    (hcj : dist c (CATZero.mid h p q) ^ 2 = 1 / 4)
    (hkj : dist k (CATZero.mid h p q) ^ 2 = 1 / 2) (hkz : dist k z ^ 2 = 1)
    (hfrac : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      t ^ 2 * (1 / 2 + 1) ≤ dist (CATZero.segment h k (CATZero.mid h p q) t)
        (CATZero.segment h k z t) ^ 2) :
    log h c k = (coneData h c).add (catZero h c)
      ((coneData h c).add (catZero h c) (log h c p) (log h c q)) (log h c z)

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.ConeData.exceptional_antipodes
lean_source.text:
/-- Source Lemma `geom:antipodal`, in an algebraic form that avoids a
local-to-global theorem in the completed space of directions. -/
theorem exceptional_antipodes (h : CATZero X) {c d x y z : X}
    (hc : T.normSq c = 1) (hd : T.normSq d = 1)
    (hdy : T.pairing d y = 1 / 2) (hdx : T.pairing d x = 1 / 2)
    (hyz : T.Opposite y z) (hz : z = T.add h c x) : T.Opposite c d

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.ConeData.five_line_fans_contradiction
lean_source.text:
/-- Final algebraic contradiction in Proposition `prop:no-configuration`.
The five line indices are AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, respectively. All geometric
input here is explicit; no Hilbert-space or associativity assumption is used. -/
theorem five_line_fans_contradiction (h : CATZero X) (ℓ : Fin 5 → X)
    (hn : ∀ i, T.normSq (ℓ i) = 3 / 4)
    (hp : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → T.pairing (ℓ i) (ℓ j) = -1 / 4)
    (hA : T.add h (ℓ 0) (ℓ 1) = T.add h (ℓ 1) (ℓ 2))
    (hB : T.add h (ℓ 0) (ℓ 3) = T.add h (ℓ 3) (ℓ 4))
    (hop : T.Opposite (T.add h (ℓ 1) (ℓ 3)) (T.add h (ℓ 2) (ℓ 4))) : False

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.ConditionalStar
OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.SamplingSequence
lean_source.text:
/-- Only combinatorial sampling assertions occur here, independent of the action
that may be chosen after the random tables have been exposed. This is not a
replacement for the random-table producer. -/
structure SamplingSequence (F : Type*) [DecidableEq F] (Admissible : Finset F → Prop)
    (L Ω : ℕ → Type*) [∀ n, Fintype (L n)] [∀ n, Nonempty (L n)]
    [∀ n, DecidableEq (L n)] [∀ n, Fintype (Ω n)] [∀ n, Nonempty (Ω n)]
    (label : ∀ n, Ω n → F → L n) where
  singleton : ∀ e : F, Tendsto (fun n =>
    ((FiniteLaw.uniform : FiniteLaw (Ω n)).map (fun a => label n a e)).totalVariation
      FiniteLaw.uniform) atTop (𝓝 0)
  star : ∀ (I : Finset F) (e : F), e ∉ I → Admissible (insert e I) → ∀ k : ℕ,
    ∃ η : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto η atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ κ : FiniteLaw (ConditionalStar (label n) I k),
        (∀ j, (κ.map (ConditionalStar.branch j)).totalVariation FiniteLaw.uniform ≤ η n) ∧
        (κ.map (fun b j => label n (ConditionalStar.branch j b) e)).totalVariation
          (FiniteLaw.uniform : FiniteLaw (Fin (k + 1) → L n)) ≤ η n

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.EnergyOrbit
lean_source.text:
/-- Actual normalized orbit points along a symmetric finite generator list. -/
structure EnergyOrbit (L X : Type*) [Fintype L] [MetricSpace X] (M : ℝ) where
  cat : CATZero X
  base : X
  isom : L → X ≃ᵢ X
  inverse : L ≃ L
  symmetric : ∀ i, isom (inverse i) = (isom i).symm
  minimum : ∀ y : X, (∑ i, dist base (isom i base) ^ 2) ≤ ∑ i, dist y (isom i y) ^ 2
  energy : (𝔼 i, dist base (isom i base) ^ 2) = 1
  bound : ∀ i, dist base (isom i base) ≤ M

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.SamplingSequence.conditional
lean_source.text:
/-- The conditional test applies to arbitrary bounded action-dependent tests,
including tests using inverses of any field labels. -/
theorem conditional {I : Finset F} {e : F} (he : e ∉ I) (hI : Admissible (insert e I))
    (σ : ∀ n, L n ≃ L n) (test : ∀ n, Ω n → (O n).Cone)
    (depends : ∀ n a b, (∀ i ∈ I, label n a i = label n b i) → test n a = test n b)
    {B : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (htest : ∀ n a, dist (O n).cone.vertex (test n a) ≤ B) :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      (𝔼 a, (O n).cone.pairing (test n a) ((O n).vector (σ n (label n a e)))) < ε

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.ConeData.conditional_test
lean_source.text:
/-- The manuscript's quantitative conditional test. The hypotheses describe
an actual finite coupling, with all of its branch and leaf errors explicit.
The action-dependent function is not required to be independent of the law. -/
theorem conditional_test {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (h : CATZero X)
    (μ : FiniteLaw α) (κ : FiniteLaw β) (v : ι → X)
    (hbar : ∀ u, (𝔼 i, T.pairing u (v i)) ≤ 0)
    (hen : (𝔼 i, T.normSq (v i)) = 1)
    (test : α → X) (letter : α → ι) (n : ℕ)
    (branch : Fin (n + 1) → β → α)
    (agree : ∀ j b, test (branch j b) = test (branch 0 b))
    {M B η : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hv : ∀ i, dist T.vertex (v i) ≤ M)
    (htest : ∀ a, dist T.vertex (test a) ≤ B)
    (hbranch : ∀ j, (κ.map (branch j)).totalVariation μ ≤ η)
    (hleaf : (κ.map (fun b j => letter (branch j b))).totalVariation
      (FiniteLaw.uniform : FiniteLaw (Fin (n + 1) → ι)) ≤ η) :
    μ.expect (fun a => T.pairing (test a) (v (letter a))) ≤
      B * Real.sqrt (1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) + 2 * M ^ 2 * η) + 2 * B * M * η

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.conditional_test_eventually
lean_source.text:
/-- Passing to the limit in the quantitative conditional test, first with
sample size fixed and then letting it tend to infinity. -/
theorem conditional_test_eventually {a : ℕ → ℝ} {B M : ℝ}
    (hbound : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ η : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto η atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ ν in atTop, a ν ≤ B * Real.sqrt (1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) + 2 * M ^ 2 * η ν) +
        2 * B * M * η ν) :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ ν in atTop, a ν < ε

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.IncidenceTemplate.exists_finite_aspherical_hyperbolic_noAction
lean_source.text:
/-- SAME-model complete construction and word-hyperbolicity. It deliberately
omits, rather than assumes, the remaining Cartan-Hadamard/deck consequence. -/
theorem exists_finite_aspherical_hyperbolic_noAction :
    ∃ K : FiniteComplex, ∃ x : K.Carrier, ∃ C : ℝ,
    ConnectedSpace K.Carrier ∧ K.Aspherical x ∧ Infinite (FundamentalGroup K.Carrier x) ∧
      0 ≤ C ∧ K.LinearDiskFilling C ∧
      NoGeometricCATZeroAction.{u} (FundamentalGroup K.Carrier x) ∧
      WordHyperbolic (FundamentalGroup K.Carrier x)

lean_source.name: OAI.HyperbolicObstruction.MainStatement
lean_source.text:
/-- A finite aspherical complex with hyperbolic fundamental group, no geometric CAT(0)
action, and no homotopy equivalent finite complex admitting a locally CAT(-1) metric. -/
def MainStatement : Prop :=
  ∃ K : FiniteComplex, ∃ x : K.Carrier, ∃ C : ℝ,
    ConnectedSpace K.Carrier ∧ K.Aspherical x ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧ K.LinearDiskFilling C ∧
    NoGeometricCATZeroAction.{u} (FundamentalGroup K.Carrier x) ∧
    WordHyperbolic (FundamentalGroup K.Carrier x) ∧
    ∀ L : FiniteComplex, Nonempty (K.Carrier ≃ₕ L.Carrier) →
      ¬ CompatibleLocallyCATNegOne L

speedup_targets.title: Flat-triangle / CN-equality propagation in CAT(0) spaces (Bridson–Haefliger II.2.9 in CN form)
speedup_targets.statement: In a CAT(0) space, if equality holds in the CN (comparison) inequality for a point z and the segment [x,y] at one interior parameter t₀ ∈ (0,1), then it holds for every t ∈ [0,1]. Equivalently, the comparison triangle of (z,x,y) is flat (BH II.2.9, Flat Triangle Lemma).
speedup_targets.reference: Bridson–Haefliger, Metric Spaces of Non-positive Curvature (1999), Prop. II.2.9 (flat triangle lemma); BH II.2.11 for the flat quadrilateral version.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about 1 page in BH (via Alexandrov's lemma and angle comparison). No Mathlib formalization; Mathlib has no CAT(0) spaces. OAI has the cone-level ingredients: `TangentCone.cn_eq_of_log_dist` (CATZeroFurther.lean:44) and `log_dist_of_interior_equality` / `log_dist_of_midpoint_equality` (TangentCone/ConeData files).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The obstruction proof's toolkit (`exceptional_identity`, `fan_identity`) does exactly this kind of propagation. From one CN equality it derives that `log` is isometric on the pair, and then CN equality along the whole segment (`cn_eq_of_log_dist`). With these in the library the target is a few lines. Caveat: this reuses the P47 proof toolkit, not the doubled-Fano design.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: med in Lean (≈10–30 lines instead of a from-scratch angle theory); low on paper
speedup_targets.confidence: medium (the OAI lemma statements match closely; not compiled)

lean_feasibility.formal_proof_to_compare: none in Mathlib; OAI's TangentCone lemmas are the nearest formal relatives

speedup_targets.title: Flat quadrilateral theorem, unit-square case (BH II.2.11)
speedup_targets.statement: If four points p,q,r,s of a CAT(0) space have squared sides 1 and squared diagonals 2, then the two diagonal midpoints coincide, and the geodesic quadrilateral spans an isometric copy of the Euclidean unit square (corner-preserving isometric embedding of [0,1]² extending the four points).
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about 1 page in BH, using II.2.9 twice. OAI already proves the midpoint part as `CATZero.square_mid` (CATZeroFurther.lean:28; about 10 lines from `CATZero.quadrilateral`).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: `fan_identity` turns a metric square plus central flatness into cone-level identities (pairing −1/4, equal `add` sums). The cone `add`/`pairing` calculus (CATZero.lean:218-505) is what one needs to build the flat square from `log`-isometries. Again this is toolkit reuse.

lean_feasibility.missing: none for the corner-isometry form; a geodesic-convex-hull definition (~40 lines) if one wants BH's exact 'convex hull is flat' form

speedup_targets.title: Fixed points of graph-model random groups for one fixed cocompact CAT(0) target (Izeki–Kondo–Nayatani; Toyoda)
speedup_targets.statement: For a fixed proper geodesically complete CAT(0) space X admitting a proper cocompact isometric action (so δ(X) < 1 by Toyoda), Gromov's graph-model random groups (with suitable expander sequences) have the fixed-point property for isometric actions on X with high probability.
speedup_targets.reference: Izeki–Kondo–Nayatani, Groups Geom. Dyn. 6 (2012), via arXiv 1012.4147 Thm 2.2 (statement verified by subagent); Toyoda, arXiv 1102.0729 (δ<1 for cocompact geodesically complete X) [Kodai 2016 venue unverified]; Izeki–Nayatani, Geom. Dedicata 114 (2005) 147–188 [unverified page range].
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Izeki–Nayatani ≈ 40 pp (combinatorial harmonic maps and the δ invariant), IKN ≈ 20–30 pp (random graph model), Toyoda ≈ 15 pp [page counts from memory, unverified]. No formalization anywhere.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The uniform conditional test replaces the target-dependent spectral constant (1−δ(X))μ₁ with a TV-coupling + Sturm inductive-mean argument whose constants do not depend on X. Caveat: P37 as formalized needs an `EnergyOrbit` with an exact energy minimizer and a uniform displacement bound M, which come from cocompactness. IKN conclude fixed points for all isometric actions on X. So the item reaches only the weaker 'no geometric action on X' form unless it is combined with Gromov–Schoen-type scaling limits (an adaptation, not reuse).
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: low–med (for the weak 'no geometric action' form only)

lean_feasibility.missing: Gromov graph model of random groups (labelled expander sequences, ~300+ lines), Izeki–Nayatani invariant δ (~150 lines), probabilistic 'with high probability' framework (~100 lines)

speedup_targets.title: Family 254: an Artin group (116 generators) with no geometric CAT(0) action
speedup_targets.statement: There is a finite-rank Artin group with no proper cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper CAT(0) space (refutes Haettel's Conjecture 1.1 / Charney's problem).
speedup_targets.reference: openai/math release family 254, preprint 'An Artin group with no geometric CAT(0) action' (2026-09-23); comparator `ArtinCAT0`.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Probably not much. 254's obstruction is algebraic: stable translation lengths, braid subgroups, sectors. It uses no random presentation, tangent-cone configuration or energy minimizer. Only the shared CAT(0) basics (`CATZero`, segments, midpoints, geometric actions) would carry over. It is useful as a near-control on the same comparator style: a big speedup here would point to shared infrastructure, not to the gadget.

lean_feasibility.missing: none (a bridge between ArtinCAT0.CAT0 and HyperbolicObstruction.CATZero, ~30 lines, if the 257 library is to be used)

open_problems.title: Gromov's question: which finite metric spaces embed isometrically in a CAT(0) space? (≥ 6 points)
open_problems.statement: Give an intrinsic characterization of finite metric spaces that admit an isometric embedding into some CAT(0) space. Known: ≤ 5 points iff every 4-point subset satisfies Gromov's ⊠-inequalities (Toyoda). Open for ≥ 6 points.
open_problems.reference: Gromov, 'CAT(κ)-spaces: construction and concentration', Zap. Nauchn. Sem. POMI 280 (2001) [unverified]; Toyoda, 'An intrinsic characterization of five points in a CAT(0) space', Anal. Geom. Metr. Spaces 8 (2020), arXiv 1907.09074, https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09074 [verified by subagent]; Lebedeva–Petrunin, '5-point CAT(0) spaces after Tetsu Toyoda', AGMS (2021), arXiv 2009.09522, https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.09522 [verified by subagent].
open_problems.status: open for ≥ 6 points (per Toyoda 2020 / Lebedeva–Petrunin 2021; not re-checked for 2022–2026 progress)
open_problems.match: The gadget is a finite configuration (points, plus midpoints and one fractional-geodesic inequality) that no CAT(0) space contains. `CoreGeometry.MetricCore` alone is a pure squared-distance pattern on 18 points: incidence = 1, two-step = 2, three-step ≥ 3. If the pure-distance core is already non-realizable, it is a new explicit obstruction certificate on 18 points.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Step 1 (Lean-checkable): ask whether `MetricCore z` alone (without `ExceptionalTest`) is contradictory in every CAT(0) space. `no_finite_obstruction` currently consumes `loose`, `missing` and `fractional` too. If it is contradictory, check every ≤ 5-point sub-configuration against the ⊠ / cycle conditions. If all pass, the doubled-Fano core is a ≥ 6-point space that the 5-point criterion misses, which is genuinely new data for Gromov's question. If `MetricCore` alone is realizable, the fractional test is essential, which is itself informative.
open_problems.payoff: med–high (new explicit data on a 20-year-old characterization problem)
open_problems.confidence: low–medium (the pure-metric core may well be realizable, e.g. in a cube complex)

lean_feasibility.statable_with: OAI `CATZero`, `CoreGeometry.Vertex`, `CoreGeometry.MetricCore`; statement `¬ ∃ (X : Type) (_ : MetricSpace X) (h : CATZero X) (z : Vertex → X), MetricCore z`
lean_feasibility.missing: none (the ⊠-inequality family needs ~30 lines if the 5-point comparison is also wanted)

open_problems.title: Are Gromov density random groups at 1/6 < d < 1/2 CAT(0)? (in particular 1/3 < d < 1/2, where property (T) rules out cube complexes)
open_problems.statement: For Gromov's density model at density d ∈ (1/6, 1/2), does the random group act geometrically on a proper CAT(0) space with overwhelming probability, or not?
open_problems.reference: Ollivier, 'A January 2005 invitation to random groups', Ensaios Mat. 10 (2005), open-problems chapter [wording unverified]; Ollivier–Wise, Trans. AMS (2011), cubulation at d < 1/6 [memory]; Mackay–Przytycki (d < 5/24) and Montée, arXiv 2106.14931, https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14931 (d < 3/14): non-trivial actions on CAT(0) cube complexes [subagent-verified]; Ashcroft, arXiv 2104.14986 and 2206.14616 (property (T) thresholds) [titles verified by subagent].
open_problems.status: open as far as found (only cube-complex actions are settled; general CAT(0) geometric actions are not) [status not re-verified on the web]
open_problems.match: The uniform conditional test exists exactly to make a random presentation fail to act on every CAT(0) space at once. 257 uses a tailored nested model (fans at N^{2−α}, tops over selected fans, decorations just below 1/2) in which the template configuration is forced in the limit.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Adaptation: (a) in the density model, find a sub-presentation pattern whose limit configuration after `conditional` + ultralimit contains a CAT(0)-impossible gadget; (b) reuse `SamplingSequence.conditional` verbatim, which only needs the `singleton` and `star` TV-coupling axioms of `SamplingSequence`; (c) verify those axioms for the density model at the given d. The hard part is (a): plain density-model presentations have no fan/top nesting.

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_feasibility.missing: density model: uniform random sets of (2m−1)^{dℓ} cyclically reduced words of length ℓ and 'with overwhelming probability' (~120–200 lines)

open_problems.title: Expanders with respect to all Hadamard spaces / a finitely generated group with fixed points for every CAT(0) space via Gromov's graph model
open_problems.statement: Is there a bounded-degree expander sequence that is an expander with respect to every Hadamard space (a uniform nonlinear spectral gap)? Equivalently, through Gromov's graphical random groups: is there a f.g. group with fixed points for isometric actions on all CAT(0) spaces built this way?
open_problems.reference: Mendel–Naor, 'Expanders with respect to Hadamard spaces and random graphs', Duke Math. J. 164 (2015) [memory; question wording unverified]; Kondo, 'CAT(0) spaces and expanders', Math. Z. 271 (2012) (CAT(0) spaces with δ = 1) [memory]; Naor–Silberman, Compositio 147 (2011) [memory].
open_problems.match: The quantifier swap 'one object, all CAT(0) targets' is exactly what P37 delivers: a barycentric (Sturm inductive-mean) control whose constants do not depend on X. IKN/Kondo show that the δ-route must fail for some targets.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Adaptation: the conditional test gives E⟨h_I, v_e⟩ ≤ o(1) for tests depending on 'past' labels. A nonlinear-spectral-gap statement needs a Poincaré inequality for all maps into X, not only energy-minimizing orbit maps. One would replace `EnergyOrbit.minimum` by an almost-minimizer from a Gromov–Schoen scaling limit and drop the uniform displacement bound `bound : … ≤ M`. The second step is the main obstacle.

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_feasibility.missing: nonlinear Poincaré constant γ(G, X) of a finite graph w.r.t. a metric space (~60 lines); expander sequence as a family (~40 lines)

open_problems.title: Does every hyperbolic group act geometrically on a Busemann-convex space (or a space with a strongly convex bicombing)?
open_problems.statement: Between CAT(0) (now refuted for hyperbolic groups by 257) and injective/Helly spaces (proved for all hyperbolic groups by Lang and by Chalopin–Chepoi–Genevois–Hirai–Osajda) sits Busemann convexity. Does every hyperbolic group act properly and cocompactly on a proper Busemann-convex geodesic space?
open_problems.reference: Lang, 'Injective hulls of certain discrete metric spaces and groups', J. Topol. Anal. 5 (2013) [memory]; Descombes–Lang, convex geodesic bicombings (2015) [memory]; Chalopin–Chepoi–Genevois–Hirai–Osajda, 'Helly groups', arXiv 2002.06895 [memory]. I did not find a problem-list citation for the Busemann version in this pass.
open_problems.match: This is the natural boundary of the device. The conditional test needs CAT(0)-specific structure: inner-product-like tangent-cone pairings (`ConeData.pairing`), Sturm's variance inequality for inductive means, and CN-equality rigidity. All of these fail in general Busemann spaces.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Adaptation sketch: replace barycenters by Busemann barycenters (Es-Sahib–Heinich / Navas) and the cone pairing by a first-variation inequality. The finite gadget would have to be re-derived from Busemann rigidity (strictly convex norms on tangent cones). The likely outcome is failure, which is still informative; see negative control N1.
open_problems.payoff: high if it works; also a sharp test of the device's limits

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_feasibility.missing: Busemann convexity (~20 lines); a library of convex bicombings (~150 lines) if the proof route is pursued

open_problems.title: Proper (not necessarily cocompact) actions: does every hyperbolic group act properly on some complete CAT(0) space?
open_problems.statement: Is there a hyperbolic group admitting no proper isometric action on any complete (possibly infinite-dimensional, non-proper) CAT(0) space?
open_problems.reference: Status context: Duchesne–Simon, arXiv 2603.03863 (2026), cited by 257 for its 'Question W' (wording not read in this pass); Monod–Py on actions on infinite-dimensional hyperbolic space [memory]. Property (T) hyperbolic groups have no proper action on Hilbert space or on H^∞ [memory].
open_problems.status: status unverified; possibly open in the CAT(0) generality
open_problems.match: The uniform test kills geometric actions. Cocompactness enters through the energy minimizer and the displacement bound M (P35), and properness of X through the ultralimit.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Adaptation: an almost-minimizer version of `EnergyOrbit` without `bound`, with rescaled ultralimits of non-proper spaces (OAI `OrbitLimit` already handles a sequence of spaces). The contradiction would then forbid all fixed-point-free actions, which would give a hyperbolic group with fixed points on every complete CAT(0) space. That is stronger than needed and may be false, so a 'proper but not cocompact' variant needs a different end-game.

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_feasibility.missing: proper isometric action without cocompactness (~20 lines, adapting `GeometricAction`)

open_problems.title: Quantitative/effective version: an explicit hyperbolic group (explicit finite presentation) with no geometric CAT(0) action
open_problems.statement: Exhibit a concrete finite presentation of a hyperbolic group with no geometric CAT(0) action, ideally with a checkable certificate.
open_problems.reference: 257 itself: 'The proof is an existence argument and does not give an effective size for K' (01-introduction.tex:15).
open_problems.status: open (new problem raised by the paper)
open_problems.match: The gadget is finite and explicit. Only the sampling and ultralimit layers are non-effective.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Make `SamplingSequence.conditional` quantitative: `ConeData.conditional_test` is already quantitative (explicit B√(1/(n+1)+2M²η)+2BMη). What is missing is a quantitative replacement for the ultralimit, i.e. a robust (ε-perturbed) version of `no_finite_obstruction`: all equalities replaced by ±ε, contradiction for ε < ε₀. That robust gadget lemma is a natural, Lean-statable sub-target.
open_problems.confidence: medium (a robust version of a finite algebraic contradiction usually exists; the work is in the constants)
open_problems.difficulty: medium for the robust gadget; high for a full explicit presentation

Grep of its build for Fano, tangent cone, barycent, Sturm, ultralimit, uniform conditional and energy found nothing. No reuse of the gadget or of the conditional test.
Per the novelty pass, no shared machinery: no Fano template, Sturm means, ultralimits or Ollivier counting.

No family in the release reuses the doubled-Fano design or the uniform conditional test. The device is single-use inside the release.

negative_controls.setting: Replace CAT(0) by injective metric spaces / Helly graphs (spaces with convex geodesic bicombings)
negative_controls.why: Every hyperbolic group acts geometrically on a proper injective metric space (Lang 2013) and is Helly (Chalopin–Chepoi–Genevois–Hirai–Osajda) [memory]. So no version of the device can rule out geometric actions on these targets. The conditional test breaks there because tangent cones have no inner-product pairing and inductive means lack Sturm's variance bound. A prover that 'proves' no-action for injective targets has a bug.

negative_controls.setting: Gromov density random groups at d < 1/6
negative_controls.why: These are cubulated, hence act geometrically on CAT(0) cube complexes (Ollivier–Wise 2011) [memory]. Any transfer of the sampling/conditional-test pipeline must lose at low density. In 257 the decoration tables sit just below density 1/2, and the template only emerges there.

negative_controls.setting: Gadget with the exceptional data removed: `FiniteObstructionData` without `loose`, `missing`, `fractional` (equivalently, the undoubled template with all Fano incidences present)
negative_controls.expected: the contradiction should not be derivable
negative_controls.why: In `no_finite_obstruction` the only route to `False` is `five_line_fans_contradiction`. Its antipodality hypothesis `hop` comes from `exceptional_antipodes`, which needs `hop` from `missing` (via `hmid`) and `hex` from `exceptional_identity` (needs `loose` and `fractional`). Without them the proof has no handle. Note that the residual data is NOT Euclidean-realizable: 5 or 6 line vectors with norm² 3/4 and pairwise pairing −1/4 have a Gram matrix I − J/4 that is not PSD. So realizability needs a genuinely non-Euclidean CAT(0) space (the novelty pass suggests cube-complex realizations). This is to be checked, not assumed.

top5.title: Pure-metric doubled-Fano core vs Gromov's CAT(0)-subset question
top5.argument: Statable now with existing OAI definitions (`MetricCore` + `CATZero`). It tests the gadget's design directly rather than its proof toolkit. One run decides whether the metric core alone is CAT(0)-impossible. If it is, and its ≤5-point subsets pass Toyoda's criterion, the gadget gives new data on an open 2001 question. This is the cleanest witness-reuse experiment available.

top5.title: Robust (ε-perturbed) doubled-Fano obstruction
top5.argument: Statable now by relaxing each field of `FiniteObstructionData` by ±ε. It is the first step toward an effective hyperbolic group and a natural test of whether a prover holding `no_finite_obstruction` reaches the robust version much faster than one without it. That makes it a measurable within-device speedup.

top5.title: Flat-triangle / CN-equality propagation
top5.argument: A textbook theorem (BH II.2.9) that is statable now. The OAI tangent-cone lemmas used by the obstruction proof are nearly the statement. It measures toolkit reuse, not the gadget, so a speedup here supports the infrastructure, not an N3 jump. It is still a clean, cheap Lean A/B test.

top5.title: Flat quadrilateral theorem (unit square)
top5.argument: Statable now, with the midpoint half already in OAI (`CATZero.square_mid`). Same caveat as S1. Expected speedup low–med.

top5.title: CAT(0)-ness of density random groups at 1/3 < d < 1/2
top5.argument: The only target where the uniform conditional test (P37) is the decisive ingredient, and the highest payoff. The statement needs about 150 lines of random-group definitions, and the adaptation (forcing a CAT(0)-impossible limit configuration in the plain density model) is the hard, uncertain part. Use it as a stretch target, not for the speedup measurement.

precedent_check.summary: No earlier construction of a finite configuration that is impossible in every CAT(0) space and built from a doubled Fano incidence graph was found. The Fano/Heawood graph usually appears in the opposite role, as the CAT(1) link of Ã₂ buildings. For the conditional test, the closest neighbours are target-dependent: IKN 2012 and Toyoda (constants through δ(X)), and Naor–Silberman / Mendel–Naor (nonlinear spectral gaps for classes of targets). An 'all CAT(0) targets' obstruction of a different kind exists: Eskenazis–Mendel–Naor, Invent. Math. 217 (2019), 'Nonpositive curvature is not coarsely universal' [memory], via metric cotype. It concerns coarse embeddings, not geometric actions, and does not downgrade the item. Nothing after 2026-10-06 using the device was found. The web search was cut short by a tool quota: two searches for a 2026 follow-up of 257 found none, and one 2026 search summary still called the realization question open, consistent with 257 not yet being absorbed.
items: IKN 2012 / Toyoda: same purpose (random hyperbolic groups vs cocompact CAT(0) targets); target-dependent constants. Not equivalent.
Eskenazis–Mendel–Naor 2019: uniform over all CAT(0) spaces, but for coarse embeddings via metric cotype. Not equivalent.
Family 254 (Artin, 2026-09-23): the same 'no geometric CAT(0) action' conclusion by a different, algebraic mechanism. Not equivalent and not a downgrade.
